message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"12","text":"The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment and investigating the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin, so that, having been checked by admonition from the one who presides, that person perhaps will not carry the sin through at all. They should turn back those who desert the ranks, so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses, in order that by the word of truth they may be able to clear away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For if they remain fallow for a long time, they become fuel for fire. They should also find out about those who are sick in body and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that its members may come forward; and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι ἔστωσαν ὀφθαλμοί","chosen":"should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment","rationale":"Preserves both the image of the deacons as eyes and their prudent movement throughout the community."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν","chosen":"investigating the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin","rationale":"Makes τίς clearly interrogative and presents the inquiry as the purpose of examining each person’s conduct."},{"source_quote":"νουθεσίᾳ καταληφθεὶς","chosen":"having been checked by admonition","rationale":"Καταλαμβάνω here describes intervention reaching or arresting the person before the contemplated sin is completed."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν","chosen":"They should turn back those who desert the ranks","rationale":"Retains the military image of leaving one’s assigned position and the restorative force of ἐπιστρέφω."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","chosen":"so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses","rationale":"Takes τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject and ἐπακούειν as the infinitival complement of ἐπιλείπειν, a defensible construction that fits the concern about continued attendance and instruction."},{"source_quote":"τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας","chosen":"the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart","rationale":"Preserves the source’s image of recurring discouragements falling upon the heart."},{"source_quote":"χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","chosen":"remain fallow for a long time, they become fuel for fire","rationale":"Retains the movement from agricultural neglect to the image of material consumed by fire."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν","chosen":"They should also find out about those who are sick in body","rationale":"Renders μανθάνω as ascertaining the condition of people whose illness is explicitly bodily."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","chosen":"bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that its members may come forward","rationale":"Understands the deacons as making the sick known to the congregation so that members of the collective multitude may appear or come forward; alternative referents remain possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","issue":"The main rendering treats τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject of ἐπιλείπειν and takes ἐπακούειν as its complement. Other defensible attachments are possible: ἐπακούειν may describe the purpose for which people assemble, with ἐπιλείπειν meaning that they fall away or become wanting; or the deacons may be the unexpressed subject of transitive ἐπιλείπειν, yielding “so that they do not abandon those who assemble to listen.” The selected construction is contextually coherent and does not require emending the supplied Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"συνπτώσεων","issue":"The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπτώσεων. The form is intelligible as the word conventionally normalized συμπτώσεων and does not obstruct translation.","proposed_reading":"συμπτώσεων","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","issue":"The plural subject is not restated. The main rendering refers it to the people whose continued gathering and listening have just been discussed, which suits the image of people becoming uncultivated through neglect. A grammatical reference to the discouragements is less contextually natural but cannot be excluded solely by morphology.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","issue":"The rare προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται allow more than one interpretation. The main text understands the sick as being brought to the congregation’s attention and the members of the collective multitude as then coming forward. Alternatively, the sick themselves may be the grammatical subject of “appear” or “present themselves.” The context supports the selected construction, but the Greek does not explicitly say “visit the sick.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"15","text":"The passengers, then, should remain stable, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiting officers should remind them of the wages. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, as a watchful bow officer, should repeat only the helmsman’s words. The Messiah should be loved as Savior and helmsman, and he alone should be trusted concerning what he says. All should pray to God that they may sail with a favorable wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction, as they sail beside a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, without clothing, and distressed, and again at another time united, gathered together, and at rest, but also seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—I mean sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive care).","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων","chosen":"The passengers, then, should remain stable, seated firmly in their own places","rationale":"Preserves both the demand for stability and the passengers’ firm occupation of their respective places."},{"source_quote":"σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν","chosen":"rocking or a list to one side","rationale":"Distinguishes general shaking from an unequal inclination of the ship toward one side."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν","chosen":"The ship’s recruiting officers should remind them of the wages","rationale":"Ναυστολόγοι denotes those who enroll or recruit a ship’s company; the recipient of the reminder is implicit, while μισθοί retains the image of promised wages or rewards."},{"source_quote":"καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς τὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","chosen":"should carefully prepare what each person needs","rationale":"Treats τὰ χρῄζοντα as the necessary provisions or arrangements appropriate to each person."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς","chosen":"as a watchful bow officer","rationale":"Πρωρεύς is the officer stationed toward the bow, while ἐγρηγορώς emphasizes continued watchfulness."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","chosen":"should repeat only the helmsman’s words","rationale":"Takes the helmsman’s words as the direct object and understands ἀντιβάλλω as giving them back or reproducing them, fitting the bishop’s subordinate role in the ship analogy."},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης","chosen":"The Messiah should be loved as Savior and helmsman","rationale":"Renders the independent title χριστός as “Messiah” and preserves both adjacent designations, σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης."},{"source_quote":"ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες","chosen":"seasick, dizzy, and vomiting","rationale":"The author’s ensuing explanation in terms of expelling disease-producing bile strongly supports a purgative or vomiting sense for the uncommon final form."},{"source_quote":"προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν","chosen":"receive the saving health that comes from attentive care","rationale":"Preserves the medical image of accepting restorative health produced by care or treatment."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ’ναῦται","issue":"The supplied print places a raised mark before ναῦται although ordinary elision does not account for it. The translation treats the mark as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature without claiming that it is an OCR error.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς","issue":"The raised mark before ἐγρηγορὼς is not required by the apparent syntax or ordinary elision. Its typographic or editorial function is uncertain, but it does not prevent a defensible translation of the surrounding words.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","issue":"The exact action of ἀντιβαλλέτω is lexically open. The main text chooses “repeat,” taking the helmsman’s words as what the bow officer gives back or reproduces. “Answer with” or “exchange” has support from conversational usage, while “relay” would fit the nautical setting but adds an unexpressed onward recipient. The selected rendering is defensible without altering the Greek.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω","issue":"The single ὡς introduces the adjacent nouns σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης without an expressed conjunction. The translation coordinates them in idiomatic English as “Savior and helmsman.” They may alternatively be heard as a combined designation, “Savior-helmsman,” or as “the saving helmsman.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐνούμενοι","issue":"The supplied form has smooth breathing. The context contrasts scattering with being united and supports identification with the unity verb conventionally written ἑνόω. This is an intelligible orthographic feature, not grounds for treating the verified print as unreadable.","proposed_reading":"ἑνούμενοι","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἀπερῶντες","issue":"The form is uncommon, but its purgative sense is made intelligible by the author’s immediate explanation involving disease-producing bile and the related form ἀπεράσαντες later in the same sentence. The exact lexical formation remains uncertain, while the contextual action is defensibly rendered as vomiting.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"16","text":"Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop toils more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, preside as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, burdened with the cares of everyone. Accordingly, in your undertaking to administer, I know that I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will give you in return the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through just administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον","chosen":"the bishop toils more than all of you","rationale":"The accusative-infinitive construction presents the bishop as bearing greater wearisome labor than every individual hearer."},{"source_quote":"ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτοῦ θλίψιν πάσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου","chosen":"each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between each member’s individual distress and the bishop’s additional burden for every member."},{"source_quote":"προκαθέσθητι βοηθός","chosen":"preside as a helper","rationale":"Combines Clement’s leading position with the explicitly stated role of helping those under his care."},{"source_quote":"τὰς πάντων φορτισθεὶς φροντίδας","chosen":"burdened with the cares of everyone","rationale":"The passive participle portrays Clement as loaded with the collective concerns of the community."},{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι","chosen":"in your undertaking to administer","rationale":"Treats σέ as the accusative subject of the whole infinitival expression: Clement undertakes the administration just assigned to him. This accords with the immediate commission and does not force σέ to be the object of οἰκονομεῖν."},{"source_quote":"ἀναφαίρετον μισθόν","chosen":"an inalienable reward","rationale":"The adjective describes a reward that cannot be removed or taken away."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ ἄκρον δικαιοσύνην","chosen":"righteousness carried to the utmost","rationale":"Preserves the expression’s image of righteousness reaching its furthest extent."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον","chosen":"to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah","rationale":"Retains the hunting image of θηρεύω, the advantageous character of the praise, and Χριστός as an independent title."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς","issue":"The main rendering treats σέ as the accusative subject of the entire infinitival expression, “your undertaking to administer,” while the nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς refer to the first-person speaker, who knows himself to have received rather than given a favor. An alternative analysis makes τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν the object of ἀναδέξασθαι, with the speaker undertaking the arrangement that Clement administer. A less contextually suitable reading takes σέ as the direct object of οἰκονομεῖν, so that the speaker undertakes to administer Clement. The explicit accusative can defensibly be the embedded subject, and the immediate commission to Clement supports that choice; no emendation is required.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"’σωτηρίας","issue":"The supplied print places a raised mark before σωτηρίας although no ordinary elision is apparent. The mark does not affect the intelligible phrase ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν πάντων σωτηρίας and is treated as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"18","text":"But you should also understand some things on your own, because he is unable to speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not have dealings with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his intention, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, laying claim to having everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his discourse. But if anyone remains a friend of those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, that person too is one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—much worse than the enemies who are visibly outside, scattering those inside while maintaining seeming friendship.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἔνια δὲ καὶ ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν νοεῖν ὀφείλετε","chosen":"you should also understand some things on your own","rationale":"Preserves the demand that the hearers infer matters for themselves rather than waiting for an explicit public statement."},{"source_quote":"ἐν φανερῷ λέγειν","chosen":"speak openly","rationale":"The phrase refers to public or unconcealed speech, contrasted with intentions that must be inferred because of plots."},{"source_quote":"προσαμιλλᾶσθαι","chosen":"have dealings with","rationale":"The verb can denote engaging, associating, or contending with someone; the surrounding language of friendship and conversation supports the broad relational rendering."},{"source_quote":"ἀλλὰ φρονίμως ἕπεσθε αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι","chosen":"Instead, prudently follow his intention","rationale":"The hearers are told to discern and conform to the leader’s will even when he cannot state it openly."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν","chosen":"laying claim to having everyone as friends","rationale":"The middle verb presents the person as asserting or pursuing a claim to the state expressed by the genitive infinitival phrase."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν διαλλάττων","chosen":"reconciling him","rationale":"Preserves αὐτόν as the explicit direct object of the active participle rather than silently changing the construction into self-reconciliation."},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας","chosen":"heeding his discourse","rationale":"The recurring singular pronouns most naturally continue to refer to the presiding leader whose intention and associations govern the paragraph."},{"source_quote":"τῇ γνώμῃ μὴ ὢν μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν","chosen":"since he is not with you in purpose","rationale":"Contrasts bodily presence with inward judgment, intention, or allegiance."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ δοκούσης φιλίας","chosen":"while maintaining seeming friendship","rationale":"Preserves the characterization of the friendship as apparent rather than genuine."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται","issue":"The main rendering understands ἕκαστος as each person who has become isolated through hostility toward the leader, and αὐτόν as the leader: wishing to retain everyone as friends, that person reconciles the leader and is saved. This follows the paragraph’s repeated singular reference to the leader and explains the communal withdrawal as pressure toward reconciliation. Grammatically, active διαλλάττων makes αὐτόν the affected object but leaves the other party to the reconciliation unexpressed. “Winning him back” or “effecting reconciliation with him” are viable contextual formulations, while identifying αὐτόν as a different alienated person is less contextually natural. The selected construction is defensible without supplying a named referent in the text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας","issue":"The main text takes αὐτοῦ as the presiding leader, continuing the repeated references to his intention, hostility, and associations. It could grammatically resume another referent assigned to the preceding αὐτόν, but the leader remains the most continuous and contextually relevant antecedent. The English retains the pronoun rather than replacing it with an explicit name or office.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"19","text":"After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and entreated me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from the life here (as is owed to me), you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother, reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, heeding the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city. Then, toward the end, do not hesitate also to disclose the cause of my death, as I said beforehand. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair. For discourse that leads astray destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν μέσῳ ἐπὶ πάντων","chosen":"there in the midst before everyone","rationale":"Preserves both the public location in the assembly’s midst and the presence of all as witnesses."},{"source_quote":"καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν","chosen":"entreated me to sit","rationale":"Construes the infinitive with the following finite verb despite the printed period, yielding the natural sense of earnestly urging Clement to take the chair."},{"source_quote":"Ἀξιῶ σε","chosen":"I ask you","rationale":"Introduces a formal request made before the assembled brothers."},{"source_quote":"σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον","chosen":"you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother","rationale":"Treats the resumed σέ as the accusative subject of διαπέμψαι and ἀναγραψάμενον. English supplies “account” and “it” from the act of writing in epitome because διαπέμπω otherwise lacks an expressed object."},{"source_quote":"μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν","chosen":"reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood","rationale":"Presents the requested record as extending to Clement’s earliest stated thoughts or reflections."},{"source_quote":"τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων","chosen":"the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city","rationale":"Retains the unusual coordination in which κηρυχθέντων grammatically characterizes both the words and the deeds."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν","chosen":"the cause of my death","rationale":"Πρόφασις can denote cause, occasion, or pretext; an account of Peter’s death supports “cause” here."},{"source_quote":"ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην","chosen":"what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly","rationale":"Preserves the necessary suffering as an obligation that the speaker has paid or fulfilled in a devout manner."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν","chosen":"no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair","rationale":"Gives the first οὐκ broad scope over the entrusting of the described kind of successor, while rendering the further explicit οὐκ εἰδώς as “without knowledge.” This yields the consolation required by the context and preserves both negations."},{"source_quote":"πλάνος γὰρ ὁμιλία","chosen":"For discourse that leads astray","rationale":"Renders πλάνος by its active force of causing hearers to wander or be deceived."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν","issue":"The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes them together as “entreated me to sit.” This treats the punctuation as an editorial feature of the supplied edition, not as proof that the Greek words are corrupt.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"συνπαρόντων","issue":"The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπαρόντων. It is intelligible as the form conventionally normalized συμπαρόντων and does not impede translation.","proposed_reading":"συμπαρόντων","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον","issue":"The main construction takes the second σέ as a resumed accusative subject after the intervening temporal clause, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with Clement and διαπέμψαι denoting his dispatch of the resulting account to James. The following section’s statement that Clement made and sent the epitome supports this role assignment. Alternatively, σέ could formally be taken as the object of διαπέμψαι, “send you,” but that would require the speaker to remain the unexpressed subject and fits the ensuing account less well. The object sent is unexpressed in Greek and is supplied in English from the writing of the epitome.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς","issue":"The main text takes the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς directly with δηλῶσαι: after the earlier request to write and send the account, Clement is specifically told not to hesitate to disclose the cause of the death near its end. It is also possible to give “do not hesitate” wider scope over both the dispatch and the final disclosure. The selected narrower attachment follows the immediate position of δηλῶσαι and yields a defensible sequence of instructions.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν","issue":"The first οὐκ can be read with broad propositional scope: it was not a man characterized as unlearned and ignorant who was entrusted with the chair. This is the main rendering and coheres with James’s resulting consolation. A strictly local reading produces “a not-unlearned man” who nevertheless is ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule, an awkward contrast. Another possible analysis distributes the first negation over the coordinated descriptions, yielding the positive sense that the successor was neither unlearned nor ignorant. The explicit second negation in οὐκ εἰδώς is retained as “without knowledge.” The ambiguity concerns scope, not an unreadable source.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς","issue":"The printed period interrupts the sequence of descriptions before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the characterization of the man entrusted with the chair. The punctuation is preserved as a disclosed editorial feature and does not by itself establish corruption or require a conjectural reading.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
